BombVault 10.7.0 backs up servers it does not run on, looks after your snapshots, signs you in through a sign-in service and brings what the web interface does to the Android app. It runs on ParleyPort 1.3.8, so a member of the group or fortress stays reachable while it reconnects.

## ✨ Added

- **Nodes.** Under **Instances**, **Add node** names the server, picks where its backups go and hands you a compose file with its key filled in. The node runs BombVault in a headless mode, needs no open port and talks to home over the relay through a private link of its own, and its backups never cross the relay.
- **Three places for a node's backups.** This instance's receiving server in append-only mode, so the node can add backups but never delete them. One of home's storage locations, with a sign-in made for the node. Or the node itself, behind a rest-server of its own, with home fetching a copy after each round. A small moving picture on each choice shows which way the backups travel, and an instance without a pairing group sets up its receiving server right from the placement step. Thanks to @LukasStipar for the reports.
- **Home runs the node.** Each node has a plan per section on its card, catches up on backups it missed while it was away, and raises one alert per failed run or time out of reach. The overview has a **Nodes** card, and **Backups** lists each node's containers and folder sets in a section of their own, where you add, edit, back up and restore them through home.
- **A rebuilt node comes back whole.** Start the same compose file on a new server and home takes the node on again, sends its placement and gives back its folder sets, container definitions and recent runs, so a missing container can be recreated from its backup.
- **Node backups can follow this instance's off-site copies.** A switch in a node's placement, Copy off site with this instance's backups, sends the node's containers and folders to the same storage locations as this instance's own, on the same schedule. There they age by the node's keep rule and stay apart from this instance's snapshots. The node card shows where the copies go. Thanks to @LukasStipar for the idea.
- **Snapshots.** The **Snapshots** page lists every ZFS, btrfs and VM snapshot on the server, with its size and who took it. You can take, rename, hold and delete them there, and before a delete it tells you how much space comes free. A snapshot that ZFS calls busy shows where it is mounted, and **Free and delete** unmounts it and deletes it while the containers keep running. Disks that are asleep stay asleep unless you ask to read them.
- **Snapshot schedules.** Under **Settings, Snapshots** a schedule takes snapshots of one dataset, subvolume or VM and keeps the newest ones. It only ever removes snapshots it took itself, never held ones and never ones you renamed, and a schedule that fails sends a notification. Each schedule is one compact row with its plan and switch, and **Edit** opens its fields.
- **No off-site copies.** If your backups should stay on the premises, switch this on at the end of **Settings, Storage locations, Off-site copies**. The off-site check then turns gray instead of red, a section with current backups reads **Protected here, no off-site copies**, and a failed or overdue backup still stands out. While it is on, the other off-site settings and the Streaming card stay hidden, and once a section copies off-site the switch goes away. ([#506](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/bombvault/issues/506), thanks @profusse)
- **Sign in through a sign-in service.** Under Settings › Security › Sign-in services you can add Pocket ID, authentik, Authelia, Kanidm, Keycloak or Zitadel next to your password. Enter its address, client ID and secret, run the test sign-in, and the sign-in page gets a button for it. For now BombVault has to sit at the root of its address for this, since under a path such as `https://example.com/bombvault/` the service can't send you back yet.
- **The address of this instance.** The Address card under Settings › Security keeps where you open BombVault from outside, such as `https://backup.example`. Passkeys and sign-in services go by it, and you can leave it empty while you only use BombVault at home.
- **Sessions you can see.** The Sessions card lists every browser that is signed in, and you can sign any of them out, or all the others at once.
- **The password check on changes.** When you signed in more than ten minutes ago, BombVault asks for your password in a small window before a change such as a new passkey or sign-in service, and then carries the change out. You can turn the question off.
- **Accounts.** People who come in through a sign-in service get an account with the role you pick for newcomers, and the Accounts card lets you change the role, block an account or remove it. Blocking, removing or demoting an account revokes the MCP keys, API tokens and OAuth grants it made, and a phone it approved stays out until someone approves it again.
- **Phones of the group always sign in.** A phone you let into the group gets its session without a switch to turn on first. A new phone still waits under Settings › Pairing until you press Approve there. A password reset ends every phone's session, and the phones sign in again by themselves. To keep one phone out, remove it on the Instances page.
- **The phone shows and starts ZFS replicas.** Replicate now, Replicate all now, the replica's backups and the ZFS servers on the Instances page show in the app, with the servers' addresses and logins left out.
- **The phone restores Compose stacks, flash plugins and database dumps.** A stack, a plugin or a dump imported into the live database goes back only after BombVault backed up the containers and the project folder, the flash or the container, and nothing is replaced if that backup fails. A dump can also be saved into a new folder in the restore folder, or downloaded at the server's own address when export encryption is on. Without it the app says where to turn it on.
- **The phone restores from an old backup folder.** Under Other sources it opens another instance's repository with its key or recovery kit and the sign-in you type, and puts every entry into a new folder inside the restore folder.
- **The phone settles anomalies.** It acknowledges a finding, marks it as expected, forgets an expectation and sets an entry's sensitivity. The old backups a finding holds stay kept until someone signs in with the password and stops keeping them.
- **The phone runs checks and keeps entries in order.** Check restore and Start test on the Verify tab, Include in schedule, Pause and Resume, Decline and Accept, tags, a ZFS sweep and Discover backups work in the app. Adding an entry stays with the web interface, since the new entry is picked from the server's folders.
- **The phone shows a locked key and what a new release brings.** The banner for a backup key that no longer opens shows in the app, and What's new for a newer release opens after Check for updates.
- **The app's settings gain button labels, the rainbow's two switches, quiet notifications and the manual.** Labels, Reactive mode and Colour rotation follow the first server's look until you set them in the app, and Quiet notifications hold for the phone alone.
- **Version and Components cards in the Android app.** The app's settings show BombVault's number with **What's new** and say where updates come from: Google Play, F-Droid, or the release page for an APK installed by hand. GlimStone's number stands in the Components card.
- **What's new in the app opens the release notes in the app.** The notes come with the app, so the window opens without a connection too and lists what the release brought, as the web's window does.
- **A waiting release's notes in the web interface.** Once **Check for updates** finds a newer release, **What's new** opens its notes in a window, with GitHub one click away in the foot. BombVault fetches the notes of that one release only, so the update check keeps its share of GitHub's rate limit.

## 🎨 Design

- **Follows GlimStone 4.9.2.** Buttons, rows, menus, tiles and tabs light up in one hover color made from your accent, and a label keeps a contrast of at least 4.5:1 under the pointer for every color you pick. Accent text keeps 4.5:1 on cards as well as on white, the keyboard's focus ring is drawn solid in the accent's text color, and the hint inside an empty field stays readable on every field color.
- **Add windows pick from shared catalogs.** Adding a storage location, a notification channel, a container registry or an MCP client opens a window of tiles with groups, a search and many more logos than before, among them Koofr, PikPak, Sia, RustFS, OpenDrive, TeleBox and Synology C2. The catch-all tile of each window stands last, and S3 compatible storage is called **Custom S3**.
- **One row per connection.** Every storage location, sign-in, container registry and notification channel is a row with its logo, a status line and its buttons at the end. A channel keeps its on and off switch in the row and opens its fields in a window behind **Edit**. A sign-in shows **Default** as a badge, and **Make default** and **Remove** sit in its window.
- **Tidier forms.** In every add and edit window the label stands on the left and its field on the right, all fields start on one edge, and the window keeps its width from the first step to the last. **More settings** stay folded until you open them, or until one of them holds a value of its own.
- **Four cards under Info.** Version, Components, Help and About. The Version card shows BombVault with its number and where updates stand, with **What's new** and **Check for updates** in one row, and says "Not checked yet" until you press the check, so "Up to date" always has a check behind it. Components lists rclone, restic and GlimStone, each number opening that project's newest release, and on a narrow card nothing gets cut off.
- **The sign-in page and the Security tab come from GlimStone.** The page has at most two buttons, Sign in and the sign-in service when one is on, with Forgot password? as a plain link below them. Your browser offers a saved passkey right in the password field.
- **The sign-in lists look like your connections.** Passkeys, sessions, sign-in services and accounts stand in the same rows as the cloud connections under Storage locations: the service's logo or the kind's glyph on a tile, the name over a quiet line, and the buttons at the end. A long passkey or device name wraps on a phone, so two that start alike stay apart.
- **A sign-in service's switch speaks for itself.** It sits at the end of the name's line, above Test sign-in, Edit and Remove, and no On badge repeats it.
- **The password question sits in the password card,** as a switch under the password.
- **Empty cards look like an empty list.** Without a password, the password card says "No password yet" over Set a password, and two-factor that is off says "Not set up yet" over Set up, the way the passkeys card does without a passkey.
- **A tidier Security tab.** The Android app card with its pairing switch is gone, since phones always pair, and the Instances card drops its line pointing to Pairing.
- **The words on the restore pictures read in the dark look.** On a picked Replace or Beside target, "Original" and "-restored" were white on the accent colour.
- **The Labels choice in the app's settings fits a phone in every language.** Where the four names don't fit, it shows their symbols alone, as the web's look settings do. "Text and symbol" was cut short.
- **The Local and Off-site switch of the dump list stays inside its card on a phone.** It ran past the card's right edge.

## ⚡ Improved

- **A login password is optional for everything.** Without one, the recovery kit, the bug report, the flash ZIP, exports with credentials, app backups, nodes and key deposits work like the rest of the interface. With a password nothing changes: these still need a sign-in at this instance, and a paired phone's session is not enough. Two-factor authentication, passkeys and OAuth sign-in for MCP clients still ask for a password first, since each is an extra way in.
- **Any password length, typed twice.** The 12-character minimum is gone from the Security page and from the reset on the login page. A shorter password gets a friendly hint that a longer one is much harder to guess, and it saves all the same. A new password is typed twice, and **Save** stays off until both entries match.
- **Nothing to set up again.** On the first start BombVault takes over your password, two-factor authentication with its recovery codes, your passkeys and the open sessions, so nobody has to sign in again.
- **Staying signed in.** A sign-in lasts 30 days, or 7 without a visit.
- **The sign-in comes from ParleyPort,** the kit your other fortress apps sign in with too.
- **The sign-in settings stay with a real sign-in.** A paired phone and a page opened from another app of your fortress can't change the password, passkeys, sessions or sign-in services.
- **Fortress apps open without a password.** The browser gets a visitor cookie of its own for the tabs it opens, so another member's pages open from **Instances** right away. Setting a password later closes those tabs, and a BombVault without a password opens from the other apps of the fortress too.
- **MCP keys and API tokens under any address.** Keys, tokens and certificate names can be made under any host name, a public one behind a reverse proxy included. Without a password the card still says that anyone who can open the page can make one.
- **A member that is reconnecting still answers.** A server or app leaves the relay for a moment when it joins a fortress, opens it again, or changes its name or address. A call in that moment, such as its status, an action or a backup asked of it, ended in an error although the member was back right after. BombVault now tries such a member again for up to three seconds, on every call, also when its address turns the connection away in that moment.
- **A renamed server is back on the relay at once.** After a new name or address, the other members listed it as gone for a second or longer.
- **Notifications through TollRoll.** When TollRoll is in your fortress and may send for BombVault, BombVault hands its messages to TollRoll first, so they arrive on TollRoll's channels even where BombVault has no channel of its own.
- **Help goes to GitHub and Discord.** The Help card under **Info** names both, and a Discord button takes the mail button's place. It opens BombVault's forum on Discord.
- **Keys work as in the rest of the family.** Only Space flips a checkbox, Home and End on a closed dropdown open its list at that end, and a typed letter jumps to the next matching option in a list or to a row of an open action menu.
- **Every instance card says what it is.** A small caption under the name reads This instance, Member, ZFS server, Android app or Node, in the same style on every card.
- **A picked option looks the same everywhere.** It fills with the accent colour, and the frame and the round dot beside it are gone. That covers the node's backup place, Storage, and the windows for restoring, removing and moving.
- **The folder picker on phones.** Its buttons stay clear of a window's Cancel and Save, and the list keeps its height while a folder loads.
- **A note when Host Data has no mount propagation.** The startup log says so once, together with what it means for disks mounted later.
- **TrueNAS setup.** The custom app in the getting started guide uses port 30624 and explains why it keeps `rslave` on Host Data: ZFS dataset backups need it, and the catalog app can't offer them.
- **Fresh building blocks.** restic 0.20.0: when a restore sets owners by name and a user or group name cannot be resolved, restic falls back to the numeric owner from the snapshot instead of handing the file to root, a restore refuses snapshots with duplicate or out-of-order names, and the index needs less memory. OpenTelemetry 1.47.0 with a security fix, x/crypto 0.59.0, x/net 0.63.0, the Docker client 0.6.3, React Router 7.18.6, Vitest 5.1.1, a fresh Node image, Gradle 9.9.1 and Bouncy Castle 1.87 for the Android app, and the latest Playwright, ESLint, typescript-eslint, Vite, PostCSS, jsdom, minimatch and Zag. The image carries Debian's security updates, among them glibc and zlib.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **A folder mounted after BombVault started is no longer backed up empty.** Without mount propagation on Host Data, as in the TrueNAS app, a disk the host mounts later looks like an empty folder to BombVault, and the first backup of an app on it recorded success with no files. BombVault now checks such a folder through Docker and refuses the backup with a failed run that says to restart BombVault.
- **Recoveries reach every channel.** A channel set to failures only also hears when a failed backup succeeds again.
- **A fortress call always goes where it belongs.** An app holding the phrase could announce an address that sent BombVault's direct call to another page of a host on your network.
- **A container with one network interface finds the fortress.** It hears the other members on your network and announces itself there.
- **Members on an old phrase are listed as such.** Members last seen in the same second as a phrase change are marked as still on the old phrase, and a member that took a new phrase no longer shows up as gone when its answer got lost on the way back.
- **Pairing is steadier.** A call whose check on a new member was cut short is dropped and can be tried again, instead of being refused.
- **Opening an older app from the fortress.** When an app in the fortress still wants a login before it opens, the message asks for an update of that app instead of a password.
- **A button that shows its words on hover stays under the pointer.** It grew while its words appeared, so in a row that wraps it could slide away, close and open again. It holds its room and the words open inside it.
- **What's new finds pages that aren't in the sidebar.** Its dot went in circles at Settings when a page such as Instances or Snapshots wasn't in the sidebar. It leads on through that page's card in Settings.
- **An action or backup asked of another member runs once.** When the answer to a direct call got lost on its way back, the call went out again over the relay, so the member could run it twice. It now ends with an error that says the member did not answer.
- **A server that reconnects is no longer listed as away.** The relay could pass on the offline notice of its old connection after the new one was up, and the other members kept it as away until it reconnected again.
- **Leaving a fortress is no longer taken for a removal.** A server that had just left could still get an answer that turned it away, and then said another member had taken it out.
- **A call that is given up keeps the relay connection up.** A call cancelled on its way out, as when its page closes, could drop the relay connection that every other call shares. A fortress closing in that moment could lose its leave, so the other members still listed the server.
- **A run's files can be browsed and restored on a phone's screen.** A container run's details did not list its files at all, because they asked for them under the wrong name. On a paired phone the restore also put the files back where they were, which the phone's session may not do, so it always failed. They now go into a new folder inside the restore folder, as in the restore window, and the question before it says so.
- **The restore window on the phone offers only what the phone can start.** It listed putting ticked files back in place and a new ZFS dataset, which the server turns down for a phone, and switches for the backup first and the ZFS safety snapshot, which the server keeps on there anyway.
- **The phone resolves failures one at a time.** Mark all resolved and resolving a group of several failures ended in an error there, so the phone leaves them out.
- **A folder set's file tree offers only what can be restored.** It let you tick the folders above the set's own path, which the restore then refused.
- **Check restore says on the phone that it runs, and what keeps it back.** Only the button's tip said the check was running, and a phone shows no tips. A check refused during a backup said so in English. The row now says that the restore is being checked, and a refusal names the section being backed up in your language.
- **What's new on the phone leaves out what the phone cannot open.** Two of its points led to the address card and to node copies, which a paired phone does not reach.
- **The password reset says that the phones sign in again by themselves.** Its texts and the docs still told you to switch phone pairing back on, a switch BombVault no longer has. The Android guide also says that saving files from the app needs a sign-in with the password, and an older server that keeps phones out now says what to do.

## 🌐 Translations

- **Every new and corrected text in all 42 languages,** and the Android guide and the corrected docs in all 26.
- **One glossary for every language.** Signing in, accounts, sessions and two-factor authentication follow GlimStone's glossary, "instance", "relay" and "storage location" read the same everywhere, and French readers are addressed with tu.
- **The docs in all 26 languages** describe nodes, the receiving server, off-site copies, the address and the sign-in services.
